advisories.title: Make the serialization test assert the serialization boundary
advisories.body: The test name says version allocation is serialized, but its only assertions cover the next version and inserted metadata. It would still pass if the advisory-lock call were removed. Assert the transaction's `execute` invocation (and preferably its lock SQL) so this test documents and protects the concurrency invariant it names.
evidence: Premise: __tests__/issued-documents.test.ts:15-22 calls persistIssuedDocument but never inspects fakeDb.execute → Improvement: the test will protect the explicit serialization invariant rather than only a single-threaded version calculation → Fix: retain the transaction execute mock and assert one advisory-lock query.
lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:21-27 → the production implementation relies on tx.execute before it reads the latest version.

advisories.title: Replace cross-boundary type assertions with shared DTO types
advisories.body: The Secretariat components discard the server-action return types with assertions such as `history as typeof notes` and `current as typeof documents`. That lets later projection changes silently reach the UI with a mismatched shape. Export the operational observation and issued-document DTOs from their action/domain modules, type the action returns with them, and consume those types directly in the clients.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:103-109 defines local shapes and then asserts both server-action results into them → Improvement: TypeScript can verify the least-privilege DTO contract end-to-end → Fix: export and use shared DTO/return types instead of assertions.
app/admin/_actions/observation-actions.ts:8-15 and app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:808-818 → both actions currently infer anonymous query return types rather than expose the client contract.

advisories.title: Split the Secretariat operational card into readable UI units
advisories.body: The newly added card combines state loading, note mutation, document downloading, and the entire expanded interface into one dense component, including a single-line nested render tree. Extract the final-documents and observations sections (or at least multiline them with named callbacks) so role-specific behavior remains reviewable and future changes do not have to modify one opaque block.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:100-139 contains fetching, mutation, download behavior, and all expanded markup in a single 40-line component with a one-line nested branch at line 136 → Improvement: isolated sections make the sensitive role-specific UI easier to test and modify → Fix: extract focused components/hooks and format their render trees normally.
app/admin/benfeitores/client.tsx:92-100 and app/admin/_components/issued-documents.tsx:8-13 → the same dense inline pattern was introduced for the other Secretariat surfaces.

suppressions.candidate: Pre-checking email existence before the unique insert can race
suppressions.note: The insert is still protected by the database uniqueness constraint and the catch returns the same opaque result; no distinct functional or maintainability consequence was established for this change.

suppressions.candidate: Missing UI error state for background operational reads
suppressions.note: The omitted error state may be worth a UX follow-up, but this lane did not establish a bounded maintainability improvement separate from the reported component decomposition.
The candidate is purely layout and does not add a non-formatter-owned clarity or behavior improvement.
